correctness.rationale: The signed chain facets are reconstructed from the union of ordinary chain polytopes over all orthants; independent sign symmetries force diagonal centered John ellipsoid. Containment is equivalent to chain sums of squared axis lengths at most one. A maximum antichain intersects each chain at most once, and n<=hw ensures the two-axis candidate is feasible. Determinant-to-KL calculation and strict positivity are direct. For n=hw a Dilworth partition into w longest chains, followed by AM-GM, globally upper bounds the determinant by h^-n. Layered-poset symmetry and concave maximization give exact equality. Exact-rational enumeration checks 1,099 finite profiles, not a universal certificate. All quantifiers h>=2, n, w, and standard Euclidean coordinate assumptions are explicit.

originality.rationale: The surveyed enriched-chain literature establishes generators, facets and Ehrhart theory, not the sharp John-ellipsoid entropy-volume estimate. A previously published exact Euclidean inradius result is used as prior work and not re-claimed. The closest John computation is for ordinary nonnegative two-level chain polytopes; the signed-chain volume computation concerns a different halfspace polytope. Classical graph-entropy minimization is a genuine possible route to parts of the characterization, but no inspected source established the precise attained KL volume lower bound. Prioritization is provisional, not global novelty certification.

Novelty of the roundness criterion considered separately may be implied by classical entropy equality theory; the specific attained quantitative KL bound is the principal assessed contribution.

value.rationale: The theorem yields an explicit sharp and attained nontrivial volume gap between the largest inscribed Euclidean ball and John ellipsoid for every imbalanced height-width profile. The lower bound is governed by binary relative entropy and comes with infinitely many exact equality families, a global roundness characterization, and exact semiaxes for all layered posets. The result is not merely an existing exact inradius or a finite computation.
